title: Effect of Tirzepatide on Health-Related Quality of Life in Japanese Patients With Obesity Disease: Patient-Reported Outcomes From the SURMOUNT-J Study

what_it_measured.text: ABSTRACT Aims: We evaluated the impact of tirzepatide on health- related quality of life (HR- QoL) in Japanese individuals with obesity disease from the phase 3 SURMOUNT- J trial.

dose.text: Written informed consent was provided by all participants prior to participation in the study. 2.2 | Procedures and Assessments Participants were randomized 1:1:1 to receive once- weekly subcutaneous tirzepatide (10 or 15mg) or placebo.

route.text: Written informed consent was provided by all participants prior to participation in the study. 2.2 | Procedures and Assessments Participants were randomized 1:1:1 to receive once- weekly subcutaneous tirzepatide (10 or 15mg) or placebo.

endpoint.text: Prespecified exploratory endpoints included mean change from baseline at Week 72 in scores other than Physical Functioning for SF-36v2 and IWQOL-L ite-C T indices.
Prespecified secondary endpoints included mean change from baseline at Week 72 in the SF-36v2 Physical Functioning domain score and the IWQOL-L ite-C T Physical Function composite score.
2 | Materials and Methods 2.1 | Study Design and Participants The study design and primary outcomes of the SURMOUNT-J clinical trial have been previously published [24].

reported_results.text: Results: Among 201 participants (tirzepatide 10mg: n=63; tirzepatide 15mg: n=69; placebo: n=69), both tirzepatide doses significantly improved IWQOL- Lite- CT Physical Function composite, Physical composite, Psychosocial composite and Total scores andtheSF-36v2PhysicalFunctioningdomainscoreatWeek72versusplacebo.Subgroupanalysesshowednomajorvariationsin treatment effect by baseline characteristics.

The least-squares mean (standard error) changes from baseline in the Physical Functioning domain score were significantly higher with tirzepatide 10 mg (1.1 [0.4]) and tirzepatide 15 mg (2.0 [0.4]) compared with placebo (−0.1 [0.4]), representing ETDs (95% CI) of 1.3 (0.2, 2.3, p = 0.022) for tirzepatide 10 mg and 2.1 (1.1, 3.2, p < 0.001) for tirzepatide 15 mg (Figure 2).

Compared with placebo, the Physical Component summary score (ETD [95% CI] 1.7 [0.2, 3.2], p = 0.024) and General Health domain score (ETD [95% CI] 3.0 [0.8, 5.2], p = 0.008) were also significantly improved in the tirzepatide 15 mg group, and the Mental Health domain score was significantly improved in the 10 mg group (ETD [95% CI] 2.5 [0.3, 4.7], p = 0.028).
CI, confidence interval; ETD, estimated treatment difference; PBO, placebo; SF-36v2, 36-Item Short-Form Health Survey Version 2.0; TZP, tirzepatide.
ETDs in least-squares mean change from baseline between tirzepatide 10 or 15 mg and placebo are shown for subgroups by (A) sex; (B) BMI; and (C) age, along with 95% CIs.
